Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the two applicable skills: the required fish-control bookshelf protocol, plus the wake-visual inspection workflow so both rollout views inform the edit. Then I’ll inspect inherited evidence before touching `solver/`.

The workspace requires a pre-edit visual diagnosis and forbids running CFD locally. I’m now anchoring both keyframe views to score, trajectory, force, and termination data—comparing the capture candidate with the most informative domain-exit failures—before consulting the bookshelf references or proposing a mechanism.

The visual comparison is decisive: all four fish self-propel with a coherent alternating wake, but the failures overshoot into an upper-boundary turn after sustained lateral drift; the capture case preserves the same carrier and instead redirects the trajectory toward the target before that exit topology forms. I’m checking the policy deltas and body-frame telemetry now to isolate which mechanism—not merely which score—caused that semantic improvement.

The inherited evidence isolates a useful scaffold: posterior-only mean curvature plus attenuation-only relief preserved thrust, reduced hard-limit residence, and improved closest approach, while scalar carrier shrinking did essentially nothing (`5.086L` vs `5.144L`, both upper exits). The captured rollout adds a response-gated posterior redirect and changes termination class. Per the bookshelf protocol, I’m consulting mechanism references before deciding how to extend that success.

The bookshelf points to one compatible extension, and I’m using it now: a continuous near-target approach mode, gated by normalized distance and measured target-aligned closing speed. It will leave the proven far-field response-gated redirect unchanged, then add modest damping and wave relief only when capture is already closing reliably. This directly targets the capture rollout’s rising `~1.1–1.3 L/T` terminal closing speed and `60.4%` posterior limit residence; it is falsified by loss or material delay of capture.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The new controller changes only terminal behavior; it retains the proven response-gated redirect elsewhere and records the bookshelf transfer block in the optimization notes. I’m moving to contract validation now, including the required dedicated check-runner; no CFD will be run.

The dedicated check-runner could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. I’m following the same checked-in runner contract directly: the exact three lightweight commands, separately, with no CFD.

All three mandated non-CFD checks pass: guidance provenance/materiality, Julia policy contract and finite action, and editable-boundary enforcement. I’m doing one final counterfactual replay of the inherited capture telemetry to confirm the new gate is identically inactive on the proven far-field trajectory and activates only during reliable terminal closing.

Produced exactly one policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds closing-gated near-target drive relief while preserving the successful far-field redirect.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:3) records visual diagnosis, hypothesis, and bookshelf transfer.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:51) now captures the reusable response-gated redirect lesson and carrier-shrink negative result.

All three mandated non-CFD checks passed: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary enforcement. The dedicated runner’s pinned model was unavailable, so I executed its exact checked-in commands directly. CFD was not run.
